notes: App-agnostic wording for the claim pipeline (#198): what Jev is asked when it categorizes observed friction, picks a target control, checks for a duplicate and grades a code-verified finding with two yes/no questions — plus the TEMPLATES the finding prose is built from. Jev only categorizes; code verifies every claim and builds the prose. The grade cutoffs are tuned on the deterministic edge-case fixtures (claims-fixtures.test.ts) only — a real-model calibration pass is still pending. Never name a specific product, route or domain term here (claim-prompts.test.ts). Bump `version` on any change.

types.destructive-unguarded: An irreversible action (delete, remove, revoke, close an account) runs at once, with no confirmation, undo or guard.
types.next-step-unclear: The page does not make the next step toward the task available or obvious, so the user hesitated, went back or gave up.
types.no-feedback: The user acted and nothing confirmed it worked (no message, no change, no progress), so they repeated it or waited.
types.blocked-action: A control the task needs could not be used (disabled, refused or broken) and the page did not say why.
types.error-unrecoverable: An error stopped the task and the page gave no way to understand or recover from it.
types.not-a-problem: The friction was expected behavior or the user's own detour (a deliberate back-navigation, a normal wait), not a problem with the page.

classify.type: The run hit this friction while doing its task: {friction}. Which claim best explains it, judged only from this screen and that friction? Choose not-a-problem when the page behaved as a reasonable user would expect.
classify.target: The run hit this friction on this screen: {friction}. Which ONE control is it about? Choose none when no single control is (a page-level wait or error).

duplicate: A code-verified finding on this screen: {finding}. Is it the SAME problem as one of the listed earlier findings — the same root cause, so the same change fixes both? Choose new unless fixing the listed one would also fix this one.

grade.need: A code-verified finding on this screen: {finding}. Do we need to fix this? Answer yes when a {persona} doing the task would be hurt, misled, slowed or blocked by it; no when it is harmless, cosmetic, a matter of taste, or not actually a problem on this screen.
grade.ship: A code-verified finding on this screen: {finding}. Do we need to fix this to complete and ship the feature "{feature}"? Answer yes only when the task cannot be completed correctly without the fix, or the product would ship wrong (for example a wrong price, or an irreversible action with no guard); no for an improvement that can follow later.

destructive-unguarded.observation: {control} on {route} acts immediately: clicking it sent {requests} with no confirmation dialog, undo or confirmation step.
destructive-unguarded.userImpact: A {persona} who clicks {control} by mistake loses what it acts on, with no chance to back out.
destructive-unguarded.recommendation: Guard {control}: ask for confirmation (naming what will be affected) or offer undo before {requests} is sent.

fact-conflict.price.observation: {route} shows {plan} at {found} ("{quote}"), but the product facts list {expected}.
fact-conflict.price.userImpact: Users see a price the product does not charge, so they decide, budget or buy on wrong terms.
fact-conflict.price.recommendation: Show {plan} at {expected} on {route}, or update the product facts if the price changed.

fact-conflict.trial.observation: {route} promises a {found} ("{quote}"), but the product facts list a {expected}.
fact-conflict.trial.userImpact: Users plan around a trial length the product does not give them.
fact-conflict.trial.recommendation: State the {expected} on {route}, or update the product facts if the trial changed.

next-step-unclear.absent.observation: {route} does not offer the intended next step "{nextStep}" (product facts): no control on the page names it.
next-step-unclear.absent.userImpact: A {persona} doing the task has no visible way to continue along the intended path.
next-step-unclear.absent.recommendation: Add a visible "{nextStep}" control on {route} as the suggested next step, keeping the other options available.

next-step-unclear.disabled.observation: The intended next step {control} on {route} is disabled.
next-step-unclear.disabled.userImpact: A {persona} doing the task cannot continue along the intended path and is not told why.
next-step-unclear.disabled.recommendation: Enable {control} on {route}, or say what must be done first to enable it.

next-step-unclear.friction.observation: On {route} the run did not take the intended next step "{nextStep}" (product facts) and hit friction instead: {detail}.
next-step-unclear.friction.userImpact: A {persona} doing the task does not find the intended path and loses time looking for it.
next-step-unclear.friction.recommendation: Make "{nextStep}" the visibly suggested next step on {route}, keeping the other options available.

next-step-unclear.observed.observation: On {route} the run could not find its next step: {detail}.
next-step-unclear.observed.userImpact: A {persona} doing the task loses time looking for how to continue.
next-step-unclear.observed.recommendation: Make the next step toward the task visible on {route}{controlHint}.

no-feedback.observation: After acting on {subject} on {route}, nothing confirmed the action: {detail}.
no-feedback.userImpact: A {persona} cannot tell whether the action worked, so they repeat it or wait.
no-feedback.recommendation: Show a clear result after {subject} on {route}: a confirmation, the changed state, or progress while it runs.

blocked-action.userImpact: A {persona} doing the task is stopped at {subject} and is not told why.
blocked-action.recommendation: Make {subject} on {route} usable, or explain on the page what is needed before it can be used.

error-unrecoverable.observation: An error interrupted the task on {route}: {detail}.
error-unrecoverable.userImpact: A {persona} doing the task is stopped by the error with no clear way to recover.
error-unrecoverable.recommendation: On {route}, say what went wrong and how to continue (retry, fix the input, or another path).
